title: CoreWeave wants customers to pay before the GPUs are fully built
friendlyTitle: CoreWeave is asking customers to pay before the computers are fully built
summary: CoreWeave's third-quarter results, as reported by TechCrunch from the company's earnings, show $3.66 billion in revenue, up 168 percent from a year earlier, a $709 million net loss, and $846 million in interest expense. The company expects about $9 billion in customer prepayments and deposits over the next three months. Chief executive Michael Intrator said CoreWeave will not fund the business with unsecured debt at current yields. Prices rose about 25 percent in July and another 10 percent later in the quarter.

whyItMatters: If you buy GPU capacity, the contract shape is changing. Intrator said short-term capacity is selling at more than $40 million per megawatt a year, against $20 million to $25 million on new four- and five-year deals. Paying up front can lock a price that looks cheap now and expensive later, or the reverse. The backlog is $132.5 billion. The demand is real on these numbers. The financing is not settled.
